name: Score or fight
what: A unit duel where each ready unit either attacks an enemy unit or scores its current health as points; first to 40 points wins.
loop: Each turn, unit by unit, you choose between cashing the unit's health now or spending it to kill an enemy unit that would score every turn. The real decision is when to stop fighting and start cashing.
changed: Hit cards hit enemy units only
numbers: Expert beats Random 100%, Greedy 93.8%, Racer 98.0%; first player 36.5% in Expert mirrors; Expert = Greedy on 48.5% of 4,787 turns (55.9% of single actions)
flags: second player (4 cards and the Coin) wins 63.5% of Expert mirrors

name: Attack and block
what: A 20-life creature duel where attackers stay exhausted through the opponent's turn and the defender chooses blockers, as in Magic.
loop: Each turn is the attack-or-hold question: attack only with units the defender cannot block profitably, and keep the rest home as blockers. Removal spells are used to take out the blocker that stops an attack.
numbers: Expert beats Random 100%, Greedy 97.3%, Racer 95.3%; first player 41% in Expert mirrors (Greedy mirror 67%); Expert = Greedy on 46% of 31,480 decisions
flags: Expert mirror games average 37 turns against 20 with Greedy, stalling into wide boards
Greedy mirror first player 67%

name: Exert to score
what: A points race to 20 where a unit scores by exerting itself, and only exerted units can be attacked, so scoring exposes it.
loop: Each ready unit chooses between scoring (points now, but exposed through the opponent's turn), challenging an exposed enemy, or staying ready. Best play scores with what the opponent cannot profitably challenge, and challenges exposed scorers it kills and survives.
numbers: Expert beats Random 100%, Greedy 93.8%, Racer 98.0%; first player 54.5% in Expert mirrors; Expert = Greedy on 48.2% of 52,551 decisions

name: Lanes and scale
what: Four lanes of facing units; each unit hits the one across from it or, in an empty lane, tips a shared scale. Five ahead wins.
loop: Each card is a placement choice: run free into an empty lane to tip the scale, stand opposite their best attacker, or kill outright. Expert blocks early, kills what it can for free, and saves Shift for the turn a lane opens.
numbers: Expert beats Random 97.3%, Greedy 73.8%, Racer 89.2%; first player 44.5% in Expert mirrors (Greedy mirror 65.9%); Expert = Greedy on 54.1% of its decisions with more than one option
flags: beats Greedy 73.8%, near the 70% line; more search did not raise it
Greedy mirror favours the first player 66%
games are short, about 9 turns between Experts

name: Front and back rows
what: A 20-life creature duel where a front row shields the back row and your life; ranged units hit the front without being hit back.
loop: Each turn is about the enemy front row: whoever empties it gets free hits on the back row and the player. Ranged units carry the game, so Expert keeps something in front and spends removal on enemy Cannons.
numbers: Expert beats Random 100%, Greedy 91.0%, Racer 98.8%; first player 46.5% in Expert mirrors (Greedy mirror 61%); Expert = Greedy on 54.8% of 34,710 decisions
flags: mana binds early and stops late: 45% of all mana goes unspent, the cap of 10 is reached on 26% of turns
the 3+3 row limit, not mana, caps the late game

name: Breaking sites
what: Three shared sites; a site scores when total power on it reaches its threshold, the side with more power taking more. First to 15.
loop: Each turn you choose which site to add power to, how much, and whether to play at all, since power near a threshold is a gift to whoever breaks it. Best play is a last-mover fight at each threshold: hold the big card until the site is one push from breaking.
numbers: Expert beats Random 98.0%, Greedy 95.5%, Racer 99.8%; first player 43.9% in Expert mirrors; Expert = Greedy on 29.3% of 3,488 turns (42.6% of single actions)

name: Blind fronts
what: Players alternately commit cards face-down to three fronts worth 1, 2 and 3, then reveal; the stronger side at each front scores it.
loop: Each placement is a read of the other side's face-down cards and energy spent, against your own hand and energy. Expert takes cheap fronts, gives up fronts the opponent paid heavily for, uses decoys, and often passes early to bank energy.
numbers: Expert beats Random 100%, Greedy 99.5%, Spread 99.5%; first player 52.5% in Expert mirrors; Expert = Greedy on 17.3% of its decisions with more than one option

name: Momentum rope
what: No units: cards shove a shared marker along a track now or add velocity that moves it every turn; reach the far end to win.
loop: Each turn you either move the marker now, change the shared velocity, or defend. Best play builds velocity when the opponent cannot afford Check or Reverse, saves Check and Anchor for their big Heave, and holds Jolts for the last round.
numbers: Expert beats Random 99.8%, Greedy 81.5%, Racer 99.3%; first player 36.6% in Expert mirrors; Expert = Greedy on 52.0% of 31,524 decisions
flags: 57% of mirror games go the full 12 rounds and are decided by which side the marker is on
first player 36.6%, leaning to the second player

name: Engine war
what: A two-player deckbuilder with a market row where points come only from Posts on your table, which the opponent can shoot. 20 points wins.
loop: Your hand plays itself, so the turn is two choices: what to buy from the row and which enemy Posts to shoot. Best play is mostly a race of Post yield, with damage bought only to deny the Post that would decide it.
numbers: Expert beats Random 96.8%, Greedy 74.3%, Racer 77.2%; first player 37.8% in Expert mirrors; Expert = Greedy on 55.6% of 4,430 turns (58.0% of single actions)
flags: beats Greedy 74.3% and Racer 77.2%, near the 70% line; racing is close to the right plan

name: Deck is life
what: A creature duel with no life total: damage burns cards off the top of your deck, and you lose when you cannot draw.
loop: Nothing blocks, so it is a race of decks: choose which enemy units are worth killing, when to cash Burn 3, and when to spend life on cards via Draw 2 or Recover. The first player hits first.

name: Open discards
what: A 30-health hero duel where discard piles are face-up and once a turn you may play a card from the opponent's for one extra mana.
loop: Each turn adds one question to the plain duel: which of his used cards to take back for one more mana, and which of yours you are about to hand him. Expert develops on curve and spends leftover mana on his pile.
numbers: Expert beats Random 100%, Greedy 83.8%, Racer 97.3%; first player 65.2% in Expert mirrors (Greedy mirror 87.4%); Expert = Greedy on 89.4% of decisions

name: Response duel
what: No board: spells hit the opponent's 20 life, and mana left unspent at end of your turn pays for a response on theirs.
loop: The whole game is one question twice a turn: spend the mana now, or hold it so every spell the opponent casts meets an answer. Expert feeds cheap Bolts to bait answers and casts big spells only into an empty or spent store.
numbers: Expert beats Random 99.8%, Greedy 96.0%, Racer 98.5%; first player 55.0% in Expert mirrors; Expert = Greedy on 46.2% of its decisions with more than one option
flags: games last 28.8 turns between Experts

name: Key pieces
what: Win by holding three different Keys in play at the start of your turn; Keys are bodies the opponent can attack, and Guards protect them.
loop: The game is denial against assembly: whoever plays a third Key gives the other one turn to break one, and Hits ignore Guard. Expert keeps its Hits for denial and plays only 0.9 cards a turn.
numbers: Expert beats Random 98.8%, Greedy 95.5%, Racer 81.3%; first player 55.5% in Expert mirrors; Expert = Greedy on 15.1% of 52,255 decisions

name: Showdown
what: Each round both buy a face-down hand with mana, the mana spent is shown, then poker-style betting with chips that are your life.
loop: Each round you pick which cards to buy knowing only the spend is shown, then bet, raise, call or fold. Expert buys strong lines when it has them, or buys a bluff that spends like a strong one.
numbers: Expert beats Random 100%, Greedy 97.8%, Caller 100%; first player 48.4% in Expert mirrors; Expert = Greedy on 54.3% of decisions
flags: both trivial bots never fold, so these numbers do not show Expert reads well (builder's caveat)

name: Prize auction
what: Sealed bids from a hand of coin cards for one prize a round; prizes are better coin or points that clog your deck.
loop: Each round is one sealed number: how much of your hand the prize is worth, given what the opponent can bid at most and what the next prize is. Expert lets point-hungry opponents overpay early and outbids on late point prizes.
numbers: Expert beats Random 98.3%, Greedy 81.0%, Racer 84.6%; seat A 52.5% in Expert mirrors (no turn order); Expert = Greedy on 25% of 19,181 bids
flags: Greedy mirror ties 85% of games (equal all-in bids)

name: Edge flip grid
what: A 4x4 grid where cards have four edge numbers and a placed card flips adjacent enemy cards with a lower touching edge; most cells wins.
loop: Every card placed is a target, so it is a waiting game over who places last next to whom. Expert places about one card a turn, passes 15% of turns, and holds Crowns for the end.
numbers: Expert beats Random 98.4%, Greedy 87.3%, Filler 97.6%; first player 65.5% in 200 Expert mirrors, 59.5% in 200 more, 62.5% pooled (Greedy mirror 64%); Expert = Greedy on 22% of 10,990 decisions

name: Supply grid
what: A 5x5 grid where you place pieces next to a chain connected to your Base; strikes compare power and cut-off pieces die. Destroy the Base.
loop: Each turn you choose where to grow, what to place, and which strikes to make, knowing any piece you destroy takes down everything hanging on it. Best play reads threats two moves deep: where can he land a 3 next to my Base.
numbers: Expert beats Random 99.8%, Greedy 99.3%, Racer 98.3%; first player 43.4% in Expert mirrors; Expert = Greedy on 18.3% of 4,173 turns (46.4% of single actions)
flags: 7 of 400 Expert mirrors are drawn

name: Round purse
what: Best of three rounds of total power, each ending when both pass, all paid from one mana purse that never refills.
loop: Each turn you play one card or pass, which really means how much of the one purse this round is worth and whether to give the round up. Best play buys each round as cheaply as possible and refuses rounds that cost too much.
numbers: Expert beats Random 99.5%, Greedy 99.8%, Spend 98.4%; first player 49.0% in Expert mirrors; Expert = Greedy on 32.7% of 24,885 decisions

name: Possession
what: A ball on nine zones; each play both sides secretly pick cards from a rock-paper-scissors table priced in stamina; most goals in 20 plays wins.
loop: Every play is a blind guess priced in stamina: the attacker needs a few won guesses to reach shooting range, then one more to score. Best play reads the opponent's pattern while hiding your own.
numbers: Expert beats Random 76.1%, Greedy 88.5%, Racer 95.3%; kickoff possession 60.4% in Expert mirrors; Expert = Greedy on 41.8% of 6,732 choices

name: Rally
what: Tennis points: a return needs reach at least the incoming shot's pace, every shot costs stamina, first to three games wins.
loop: A point is a stamina-for-tempo trade: Pace 5-6 shots win at once for 3-4 stamina unless the other side holds the one card that answers, while cheap shots keep the rally going. Games are often decided when one side hits 0 stamina and loses serves it cannot pay for.
changed: serve passes after every point instead of every game
numbers: Expert beats Random 96.8%, Greedy 94.3%, Saver 69.5%; first server 48.5% in Expert mirrors (Greedy mirror 46%); Expert = Greedy on 37.0% of 37,148 decisions

name: Range duel
what: Two fighters on a seven-space line secretly pick moves at once; speed decides who acts first, range whether it hits, energy pays. 12 life each.
loop: Both fighters close to distance 1 and the duel becomes a speed guess: Jab cancels slower attacks, Punch beats Kick or Lunge, Guard blanks the big hit. The decisions are distance and speed reads.
numbers: Expert beats Random 98.5%, Greedy 84.5% (no Racer); fighter A 47% in Expert mirrors (no first player); Expert = Greedy on 31% of 8,301 moves
flags: energy almost never binds: at the cap of 6 in 93% of decisions

name: Bust duel
what: Each round both draw cards into face-up lines, stopping before strain busts them; the higher line hits the other, then each buys a card.
loop: Each draw you choose push or stop with the opponent's line in plain sight, then buy one card with your line's power. Expert stops early when it acts first and buys deck control rather than raw power.
numbers: Expert beats Random 100%, Greedy 98.5%, Pusher 99.0%; first player 47.8% in Expert mirrors; Expert = Greedy on 75.3% of 104,007 decisions
flags: round damage is capped at 5 and coin past 7 buys nothing more

name: Curling line
what: Stones on a one-dimensional sheet push the first stone in their path; closest to the mark scores, and the scorer throws first next end.
loop: Each throw is a free Lag or Guard in front, a draw to a cell in the House, or a hit that pushes a stone out, paid from 5 energy. Best play is the hammer: the side throwing last converts the end.
numbers: Expert beats Random 99.6%, Greedy 100% (no Racer); hammer in end 1 wins 66.7% of Expert mirrors, 64.5% on 400 more, 65.6% pooled; Expert = Greedy on 58.2% of 38,911 throws

name: Hidden runner

loop: The Runner picks a move kind each round knowing the kind is announced; the Hunter narrows the possible nodes and closes in. After any exact sighting the Hunter pounces, so a sighting ends the game instead of starting a chase.

name: Claims

name: Hidden contracts
